To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the immunosuppressant FK-506 inhibitory effects on T-cell activation are exerted by blocking a step in the activation pathway that requires the provision of an extracellular calcium signal and concurrent activation by phorbol myristate acetate (PMA) of a protein kinase C-like enzyme.

(1) the mechanism of action of FK-506 is to inhibit the activation of a Ca2+/calmodulin-dependent phosphoprotein phosphatase, calcineurin, which is a key event in the activation of lymphocytes by mitogenic combinations; (2) calcineurin activity is regulated by a protein kinase C-mediated phosphorylation event; and (3) calcineurine inhibition is the basis of the immunosuppessive activity of FK-506.
FK-506 inhibitory action is completed early in lymphocyte activation and is accelerated as protein kinase C activation is increased.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the mechanism of action of FK-506 and the role of the FK-506 binding protein in the regulation of lymphocyte activation.
the molecular mechanism of action of immunosuppressant drugs.
the molecular mechanism of action of a novel immunosuppressant, FK-506, and the role of the T-cell receptor in T-cell activation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
FK-506 acts to prevent the completion of a step in lymphocyte activation that is completed early in response and requires both a Ca2+ and protein kinase C signal.
the immunosuppression by FK-506 results from inhibition of the signal transduction process that couples the Ca2+ signal to the activation of protein kinase A.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
FK-506 inhibitory activity correlates with the ability of the agent to suppress Ca2+ influx in lymphocytes.
the immunosuppressant FK-506 acts by inhibiting a step in the early events of T-cell activation.
the FK-506 binding protein is a component of a protein kinase C-dependent signal transduction pathway that is essential for the initiation of lymphocyte activation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the FK-506 binding protein (FKBP) is a key component in the mechanism of action of immunosuppressive agents such as FK506, rapamycin, and cyclosporine.
the FK-506-sensitive event is the induction of a protein kinase cascade that mediates the activation of transcription factors and the induction of gene expression.

FK-506 inhibitory effects are exerted on an early event that is common to the induction of lymphocytes to proliferate in response to a wide variety of stimuli and that the event is completed early in response to the stimulus.
